ruling.recommended_action: Refund SGD 5.22 (excess distance fare = 2.886 km × $1.81/km) to the rider's original payment method; do not refund time fare, platform fee or tolls; issue the driver a notification-duty reminder and log the notice failure on his route compliance record (RD-7, first infraction, no formal warning); no account flag (no prior upheld deviation in 90 days).
ruling.reasoning:
Route deviation: actual 13.51 km vs recommended 10.624 km → deviation 2.886 km, above the 1 km tolerance (RD-1). The GPS track (system record, overriding the rider's "never agreed" and the driver's statement) shows the driver drove the recommended corridor (Kent Ridge Rd → Buona Vista → AYE → Central Expressway → Merchant Rd → Church St) to ~9.2 km, then left it around 09:01 by looping north via Tiong Bahru Rd → Alexandra Rd → Prince Charles Crescent → Lower Delta Rd → Jln Bukit Merah before rejoining the recommended path on the Central Expressway at ~09:07 (lat 1.2829, lng 103.8349) — approximately 5.4–5.5 km of off-route driving (vs ~2.7 km on the recommended path over the same stretch), i.e. ~2.9 km of excess distance, consistent with the 2.886 km total deviation.

Traffic reason (RD-4) is not established: the only traffic speed-band records are on the AYE (band 2) — and the AYE is the route both the recommended path and the driver used through that window — and on the Central Expressway (band 7). The replaced recommended portion (the City/Yeo Chu Kang end of the AYE and the Jln Bukit Merah/Bernam corridor) has no incident or closure event and no recorded speed band 1–2 during the segment (08:57–09:04), so the reroute is not traffic-justified. The recorded call (08:47:50, 25 s, no recording_ref, no transcript) and the driver's "she said ok" are a claim, not consent: there is no in-app chat, no call recording, and the only pre-trip call has no verifiable content, so rider consent to "via Prince Charles Crescent" is unproven (RD-5) — the driver's own words are the only content source and do not decide it. The rider's complaint ("he never agreed a different route with me") is met with no documentary counter-evidence, so no segment is exempt.

Amount: excess distance fare only (RD-2). Per-km rate = distance fare ÷ actual distance = $19.05 ÷ 13.51 km = $1.8098/km. Refundable km = 2.886 km. Refund = 2.886 × $1.8098 = $5.22. Time fare ($5.07), platform fee ($1.47, booking fee, not surged), and tolls ($0) are not refunded; surge 1.0 (no differential). Under $10 → system decides (TH-1, C1), precedent DISP-2026-0089 (uninformed reroute).

Safety screen: no threat, harassment, sexual remark, dangerous-driving allegation or accident in any chat, call record, statement or complaint → escalate = false, safety_concern = none. Evidence: sufficient — GPS coverage is continuous (thinned but complete), fare breakdown, timings and the call log are all present; the only unresolved reading (call content) is a claim-vs-record conflict resolved against the claimant under RD-5. No prior upheld deviation in 90 days → no flag.

segment_findings.reason: Driver left the recommended AYE/Jalan Bukit Merah–Central Expressway corridor from ~09:01 to ~09:07 and looped via Tiong Bahru Rd → Alexandra Rd → Prince Charles Crescent → Lower Delta Rd → Jln Bukit Merah, ~5.4 km of off-route driving (~2.9 km excess). No traffic reason under RD-4: the AYE (the only band-2 link) is the corridor both routes used, and the Central Expressway is band 7; the replaced recommended portion had no incident or band 1–2 during the segment. Consent to 'go via Prince Charles Crescent' is claimed only in the driver's statement; the recorded call has no recording_ref or transcript and no pre-trip chat exists, so under RD-5 the named-road agreement is unproven (a driver's word alone is a claim, not consent) and the segment counts. Not exempt → refund of the excess distance fare under RD-2.

element_findings.reason: Only band-2 record is on the Ayer Rajah Expressway, the corridor both the recommended route and the driver used; the Central Expressway (the rejoined link) is band 7. No closure, accident or congestion event on the replaced recommended portion (southern AYE / Jln Bukit Merah–Bernam corridor) during the off-route window 08:57–09:04.

element_findings.element: Rider notice and consent to the named road 'Prince Charles Crescent' (RD-5)
element_findings.reason: Notice was claimed by phone: the one recorded call (25 s) has recording_ref null, transcript null and details null, and there is no chat log at all. RD-5 requires the call recording to prove verbal notice/acknowledgement; the driver's uncorroborated assertion is a claim. Contrast DISP-2026-0089 (uninformed reroute) — treated as uninformed.

element_findings.element: Rider's filed claim that no route was agreed and the meter exceeded the estimate
element_findings.reason: Supported by the GPS deviation of 2.886 km beyond the recommended route with no verified consent or traffic justification; the excess distance fare is refundable.
No threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark, dangerous-driving allegation, accident or expression of feeling unsafe anywhere in the record; screening complete, no escalation.

rejected_claims.reason: The driver asserts the rider said 'ok' to going via Prince Charles Crescent. The supporting call record carries no recording_ref, transcript or details; no in-app chat exists. Under RD-5 verbal consent needs a call recording — the driver's own statement is a claim, not evidence, so consent is not established.

The driver's claimed jam on the Ayer Rajah Expressway is not the replaced corridor: the recommended route itself runs along the AYE, and the only band-2 record is on that shared AYE link. No RD-4 traffic reason applies to the replaced portion, so the reroute cannot be excused.
